title: Positional Language Play
strapline: Under the table, behind the tree, in the box, next to a friend — maths you learn with your whole body.
intent: Children learn and use positional language — under, over, behind, in front, next to, between, through.
Children develop spatial awareness by moving their own bodies and objects through space.
Children follow and give directions, listening carefully and being precise.
Children explore inside and outside, full and empty, near and far through play.
Children build the spatial reasoning that underpins later maths, map-reading and writing.
implementation: Build an obstacle course to go under, over, through and around, narrating every position as they move.
Play hiding and treasure games where the clue is the position — 'behind the bin', 'under the mat'.
Give and follow simple direction games — 'put teddy on the chair, now under it, now next to you'.
Use small-world and construction to place objects precisely and describe where they are.
Weave positional talk into everyday routines — 'coat on the peg', 'cup next to your plate'.
Let children be the direction-giver, choosing and saying the positions for others to follow.
Add barrier games — two children, a screen — where one describes positions for the other to copy.
key_questions: Where is teddy now — can you tell me exactly?
Can you go under the bridge and then through the tunnel?
Where shall we hide it — behind, under or on top?
Put the car next to the tree — now where should it go?
How could you tell your friend exactly where to put it?

impact.text: Children learn and use positional language — under, over, behind, next to, between, through.
Children develop spatial awareness moving their bodies and objects through space.
Children follow and give precise directions, listening carefully.
Children explore inside and outside, full and empty, near and far in play.
Children take the direction-giver role, choosing and naming positions for others.
Children place objects precisely in small-world and construction and describe where they are.

enhancements: An obstacle course to go under, over, through and around.
Hiding and treasure games with position-word clues.
A teddy and props for follow-the-direction games.
Barrier-game screens for describing and matching positions.
Small-world layouts for placing and describing objects.
Tunnels, boxes, arches and bridges for whole-body position play.
Positional-word picture cards to prompt the language.

playing_exploring: Children learn position through their whole moving bodies.
They explore in, out, under and over by climbing, hiding and posting.
active_learning: Children concentrate to follow a string of directions correctly.
They persist to describe a position precisely enough for a friend to copy.
creating_thinking: Children choose their own hiding places and reason about position.
They work out how to give directions clearly and adjust when a friend gets lost.
